title: RuView help
summary: Connect a configured source, understand its limits, and manage local recordings. Reading help does not start sensing or change a recording.

topics.title: Start here
topics.summary: Use this workspace to view receive-only sensing and the controls your source supports.

sections.heading: Before you connect
paragraphs: Use a source you are authorized to observe. RuView upstream and CC-native CSI are separate providers with different capabilities.
A reading is an estimate from its named source. It is not a person's identity or a medical result.
steps: Choose a configured profile.
Check the provider, source mode and capability labels.
Use an enabled control only when its status is current.

sections.heading: Read without changing anything
paragraphs: Help and the walkthrough do not connect, calibrate, start recording or delete data. You choose those actions in the workspace controls.

topics.title: Choose a profile and connect
topics.summary: Use an existing configured profile for the RuView upstream service.

sections.heading: Connect to the intended source
steps: Open the connection controls and load the configured profile list.
Choose the intended enabled profile. Check its name before connecting.
Connect, then wait for a current connected status.
paragraphs: A disabled or missing profile cannot be used here. Ask the person who manages Cyber Controller to configure it. Do not paste a service URL, password or token into this screen.
Connecting attaches to the configured sensing service. It does not mean a local sensor or model has become available.

sections.heading: If connecting fails
paragraphs: Keep the selected profile in view. Read the status and use the recovery help. Repeated clicks do not fix an authentication or capability problem.

topics.title: Understand availability
topics.summary: A supported feature can still be unavailable right now.

sections.heading: Read the labels
bullets: Available means the source currently reports that capability available. The corresponding control must also be enabled.
Unavailable means the capability is known but cannot be used now. Refresh current state and read the reason.
Unsupported means this provider does not offer the feature. Changing a checkbox cannot add it.
Missing status means availability is not established. Do not treat an absent reading as a zero.

sections.heading: Keep providers separate
paragraphs: Switching the viewing provider changes which readings you inspect. It does not give CC-native CSI the upstream provider's capabilities.
CC-native CSI does not support pose, imaging, through-wall imaging, biometric identification, multi-person separation or metric tracking. An upstream estimate does not remove those limits.

topics.title: Sensing is different from a scan
topics.summary: This workspace shows receive-only sensing from a configured source.

sections.heading: Know what the view represents
paragraphs: This view does not scan for networks or devices, identify people, or transmit radio signals.
Live, replay and simulation are different source modes. Replay shows recorded data. Simulation is generated data. Neither is a new live observation.
Check the provider, last-received time and stale labels before interpreting a change.

sections.heading: Treat estimates as estimates
paragraphs: Pose and vital-sign views, when supplied by RuView upstream, are non-diagnostic estimates. They do not establish identity, health or sensing accuracy.
A missing value means not reported or unavailable. A displayed zero is meaningful only when the source actually reports a current value.

topics.title: Use models and profiles
topics.summary: Use only model and profile choices the connected source actually supports.

sections.heading: Choose an existing model
steps: Check the current provider and model availability.
Select an existing reported model or configured profile.
Use an enabled action and wait for its reported result.
paragraphs: An accepted click is not proof that weights were loaded or a profile was applied. Check the resulting model status.

Model download, arbitrary file paths, training-job management and unsupported activation actions are not provided by help. Some model controls can remain unavailable even when the source reports model support.

sections.heading: Keep calibration separate
paragraphs: Loading or choosing a model does not calibrate the room. Use calibration only when its own control is available.

topics.title: Calibrate the intended setup
topics.summary: Calibration belongs to a specific source, room setup and set of sensors.

sections.heading: Start deliberately
steps: Check that the connected source and sensor selection are the intended ones.
Use the calibration control with the current confirmed setup.
Wait for the reported calibration state before finalizing or cancelling.
paragraphs: Do not guess a missing setup or session. If the screen cannot establish the current calibration, leave the action unavailable.
Finalizing calibration, cancelling unfinished calibration and resetting saved calibration are different actions. Read the confirmation before resetting.

sections.heading: When the setup changes
paragraphs: A new source, restarted service or changed sensor setup can make an earlier calibration unsuitable. Check the current state before reusing it.
Calibration does not add unsupported capabilities or make estimates diagnostic.

topics.title: Start a local recording
topics.summary: Recording starts only after your explicit action.

sections.heading: Before starting
steps: Check that the intended upstream source is connected and current.
Review the local recording policy and available capacity.
Use Start recording once, then wait for the confirmed recording result.
paragraphs: Keep the confirmed recording identity with that recording. Stop and any retry must refer to the same recording.
If the result is uncertain, inspect current state before doing anything else. Do not assume that a timed-out start failed.
If local retention or safe recording state cannot be established, capture stays unavailable. Help cannot enable it.

sections.heading: Where it stays
paragraphs: Recordings stay in the configured local store until you manually delete them. Starting a recording does not enable automatic export or expiry.

topics.title: Stop the recording you started
topics.summary: Stopping ends capture and preserves the retained recording.

sections.heading: Stop the same recording
steps: Use the Stop control for the recording whose start was confirmed.
Wait for the reported terminal result.
If a retry is needed, keep the same recording identity.
paragraphs: Never switch a delayed stop to whichever recording is active now. If the screen has lost the original identity or reports a mismatch, leave Stop unavailable and inspect the retained recordings.
Stopping a local wait, closing help, disconnecting a view or closing the browser is not confirmation that capture stopped.

sections.heading: After stopping
paragraphs: Check the retained recording list and final result. Stopping does not delete the recording.

topics.title: Inspect retained recordings
topics.summary: Use the reported local list to distinguish retained recordings from current capture.

sections.heading: Check what was retained
steps: Open the recording controls and inspect the reported retained list.
Match the recording identity to the start and stop results.
Check the reported status and limits before replay or deletion.
paragraphs: An unavailable list is not an empty store. Refresh current state before deciding that a recording is missing.
A stale list can describe an earlier state. Do not infer a successful stop or deletion from it.
Help does not browse raw filesystem paths or export recordings. If the list control is unavailable, it stays unavailable here too.

topics.title: Delete one retained recording
topics.summary: Manual deletion permanently removes the exact recording you confirm.

sections.heading: Confirm the exact target
steps: Inspect the current retained list.
Select the intended retained recording and check its identity.
Read the deletion confirmation, then explicitly confirm that recording.
Wait for the result and refresh the retained list.
paragraphs: Do not use a stale selection, guess a missing recording, or delete to resolve an uncertain stop.
If the target or its retained state cannot be confirmed, deletion stays unavailable.
Capacity limits never authorize automatic deletion of an older recording.

topics.title: Understand recording limits
topics.summary: At capacity, capture stops or is rejected without deleting retained data.

sections.heading: Product limits
bullets: Up to 64 retained recordings and 1 GiB of retained data in total.
Each recording is bounded by 128 MiB, 100,000 frames and 15 minutes.
The first reached limit can stop capture. A completed recording can report that capacity was reached.

sections.heading: Make space deliberately
paragraphs: Inspect the retained list. Manually delete only recordings you no longer need, with confirmation of each exact target.
Do not keep pressing Start when capacity is reached. A limit does not trigger export, automatic expiry or deletion.
A storage or retention problem can keep capture unavailable until the application can establish safe current state.

topics.title: Keep sensing and recordings local
topics.summary: Choose the intended source and keep credentials out of browser-visible content.

sections.heading: Local recording policy
paragraphs: Recordings remain local until explicit manual deletion. There is no automatic capture, export, expiry or deletion.
This help feature does not save walkthrough progress, profile choices or search text to browser storage. It sends no telemetry or product commands.

sections.heading: Protect the source
paragraphs: Use only a configured profile you are authorized to observe. Service credentials belong in the private configuration, not in help, screenshots or shared logs.
The view does not identify people. Upstream estimates are not medical results.

topics.title: Recover from stale or failed state
topics.summary: Restore a current observation before repeating an action.

sections.heading: Stale, offline or timed out
steps: Check the browser connection and the workspace status.
Refresh state and wait for the provider's current reading.
If an action's result is uncertain, inspect its state before retrying.
paragraphs: Last-known values can stay visible while updates are unavailable. A stale reading is not a current observation.
Retry a stop only for the original confirmed recording. Do not replace an uncertain target with a newer one.

sections.heading: Authentication or unavailable state
paragraphs: If Cyber Controller asks you to sign in, sign in again and reload the page. Do not paste a token into a browser field.
If the source reports an authentication error, check the configured profile with the person who manages it.
If refresh still cannot establish current state, leave affected actions unavailable. Do not manufacture a missing result or bypass a disabled control.

topics.title: Finish and leave the workspace
topics.summary: Confirm ongoing work before disconnecting or leaving.

sections.heading: Finish deliberately
steps: Check for a recording or calibration that is still in progress.
Stop the exact recording you started, or finish or cancel the intended calibration through its own control.
Wait for the reported result and inspect retained recordings if needed.
Disconnect the intended upstream profile when you are ready to detach.
Close the workspace.
paragraphs: Closing help only closes help. Closing the page or cancelling a local wait is not a confirmed stop of an upstream action.
Disconnecting does not delete recordings. It does not shut down an independently operated sensing service.
